description: We are high school students passionate about engineering, space exploration, AI, and technology. We want to use NASA's data to solve real-world problems and develop innovative solutions. We are looking for teammates skilled in programming, AI, data science, app development, astronomy, or design. We value creativity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn. If you're excited about space and innovation, join us!
summary:
**MISSION CONTROL** is an interactive, browser-based space mission simulator that allows users to experience the engineering decisions involved in designing and operating spacecraft.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming complex space mission concepts into an engaging, hands-on experience. Players assemble satellites, select scientific instruments, design orbital trajectories, manage mission budgets, and operate spacecraft to complete scientific objectives.

The simulator features Earth observation and lunar reconnaissance missions, including agricultural monitoring in California's Sacramento Valley and a time-sensitive wildfire observation mission. Using NASA imagery and physics-based calculations, players must account for orbital mechanics, spacecraft mass, power consumption, imaging opportunities, and communication windows.

Unlike traditional educational games, MISSION CONTROL emphasizes realistic engineering trade-offs and consequences. A successful mission requires more than collecting data; players must also transmit it back to Earth.

By making aerospace engineering interactive and accessible, MISSION CONTROL helps students develop problem-solving skills, understand the complexity of space exploration, and explore potential careers in STEM.
details:
MISSION CONTROL is an interactive spacecraft engineering and mission simulation game designed to give users hands-on experience with the challenges of space exploration. Instead of simply learning about spacecraft, players make the engineering decisions required to design, plan, operate, and evaluate a space mission.

How It Works

Players begin by selecting an Earth observation or lunar reconnaissance mission. They can assemble a spacecraft using components such as solar panels, batteries, cameras, and communication systems. Each component affects the spacecraft's mass, power requirements, capabilities, and overall cost.

Next, players plan their mission by selecting orbital parameters and evaluating predicted imaging opportunities, sunlight exposure, battery consumption, and ground-station communication windows. During flight, they operate the spacecraft, capture simulated observations, and transmit collected data back to Earth. At the end, they receive a mission review comparing predicted and actual results.

Technology and Development

We developed MISSION CONTROL as a browser-based application using TypeScript, React, CSS, and Three.js for interactive 3D spacecraft visualization. We used NASA Blue Marble imagery for geographic visualization and incorporated mathematical models of orbital motion, spacecraft power, and communication opportunities. GitHub supported version control, and Cloudflare Pages was used to deploy the application publicly.

Creativity and Engineering Challenges

What makes MISSION CONTROL unique is its emphasis on interconnected engineering decisions. Players cannot succeed simply by selecting the correct answer. They must balance scientific objectives against practical constraints such as spacecraft mass, available energy, orbital geometry, communication access, and mission budgets.

For example, our California Wildfire Observation mission challenges players to acquire and deliver a simulated visible-light observation within six hours. Capturing the observation alone is insufficient; the data must reach Earth before the deadline.

Throughout development, we prioritized scientific accuracy within the simulation's stated assumptions, accessibility for beginners, intuitive controls, and meaningful consequences for player decisions. We also distinguished historical NASA background imagery from simulated scientific observations.

Impact

Our goal is to make aerospace engineering more accessible, especially to students who may not have experience with spacecraft design or orbital mechanics. By combining interactive gameplay with engineering principles, MISSION CONTROL encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, and an understanding of how real space missions involve multiple interconnected systems.

Ultimately, we hope MISSION CONTROL inspires more students to explore aerospace engineering, physics, computer science, and space exploration.
